title: prefill/decode: chunked speculative prefill + kernel scheduler + KV-cache batching optimizations
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and improve throughput for mixed-length workloads by overlapping prefill and decode stages, enabling chunked/speculative prefill, and upstreaming a lightweight kernel scheduler that prefers locality-friendly kernels. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) chunked prefill path to break large prefill requests into speculatively decoded chunks so that the decode pipeline can start earlier; 2) speculative prefill which issues tentative decode work for high-confidence prefix completions and rolls back if hypotheses mismatch; 3) a kernel scheduler that picks kernels by sequence-length distribution and KV-cache locality and introduces a micro-batching policy to reduce kernel-switch overhead. Changes include runtime plumbing to track speculative tokens, eviction-safe KV-cache checkpoints, and metrics/tracing for overlap efficiency. Testing: unit tests for checkpoint/rollback semantics, end-to-end perf canary harness with 1k synthetic traces, and regression test against canonical QA prompt sets. Rollout: feature-flag gated, default off for dedicated/private until validated; gradual rollout to hosted with canary config. See commits and files_changed for details.
